text: Round one, the slow way: walk down the dates with ↓ until you reach the last one, A61.
teach: The arrow keys move the active cell one cell per press — feel how long sixty rows takes.

text: Round two: back to the top with Ctrl+Home, then the same trip in one Ctrl+↓ — the Name Box reads A61.
teach: Ctrl+Home returns to A1 and Ctrl+Arrow jumps to the edge of the data in one press; the Name Box, left of the formula bar, shows the cell you landed on.

text: Take the two dates above with Shift+↑, then the whole date column in one Ctrl+Shift+↑: the selection reads A1:A61.
teach: Shift+Arrow grows a selection one cell per press; add Ctrl and the same jump selects to the edge in one press.

text: Walk the tabs to Costs and land on the Domain total E4: the grid shows a number, the formula bar shows =B4+C4+D4.
teach: A workbook is the file and the tabs along the bottom are its sheets: Ctrl+PgDn / Ctrl+PgUp walk them, and the formula bar shows what the active cell really holds.

text: Sheet2 is the associate’s inputs scratch — go there and rename it Inputs.
teach: Rename Sheet, Home › Format (Alt, H, O, R), opens the active tab’s name: type the new one and press Enter.

text: Old wk37 is a dead half-export — delete it and confirm.
teach: Delete Sheet (Alt, H, D, S) removes the active sheet; Excel asks first, because a deleted sheet cannot be undone.

text: Insert the sheet the weekly report will live on and rename it Report.
teach: Shift+F11 inserts a new worksheet in front of the active one and makes it active.

text: The report reads first: move Report to the front of the workbook.
teach: Move or Copy Sheet (Alt, H, O, M) moves the active sheet: ↑ ↓ pick where it will sit, Enter confirms.

text: Open the Ribbon with Alt, step into Home › Font, then back all the way out with Esc.
teach: Alt shows KeyTips: every tab and command has a letter, and Esc backs out one level at a time.

text: Walk to the View tab with Alt, W, look at what lives there, and leave with Esc.
teach: The tab letters never change: H Home, N Insert, P Page Layout, M Formulas, A Data, W View.

text: Report is a page someone reads: turn its gridlines off.
teach: View › Show › Gridlines (Alt, W, V, G) toggles the grid on the active sheet only.

text: Open Format Cells with Ctrl+1, glance at its tabs, and close it with Esc.
teach: Ctrl+1 opens Format Cells from anywhere — the dialog behind most formatting.

text: Open the same dialog the long way, Alt, H, O, E, and close it again.
teach: Every dialog also has a Ribbon route — Format Cells is Home › Format › Format Cells, Alt, H, O, E.

text: Press F9 once — on Automatic it is instant, and your hands should know it.
teach: Calculation is Automatic here; F9, Calculate Now, is the key you live on when a big model goes Manual.

text: Open Excel Options and enable iterative calculation.
teach: Alt, F, T opens Excel Options; on the Formulas page, I enables iterative calculation, which circular models need.

text: Add Font Color to the Quick Access Toolbar.
teach: Q opens the Quick Access Toolbar page: ↑ ↓ pick a command, A adds it, Enter is OK.

text: Add Fill Color the same way.
Add Borders.
Add Decrease Decimal, the last of the four.
Run one from the keyboard: Alt, then 2 — Undo, straight off the toolbar.
teach: Alt alone numbers the toolbar 1–9; Alt then the number runs that command from anywhere.

text: The inputs scratch needs an owner’s pass: move to the Inputs sheet.
Add the units line: type USD unless stated into A2.
teach: Type and press Enter to commit; every pack page states its currency once, near the top.

text: Color the typed figures blue — the margin target B5 and the kWh estimate B6.
teach: House rule: anything typed is blue, anything calculated stays black, so a reviewer sees the drivers at a glance.

text: The wholesale price deserves its own cell: type 0.13 into B4 and color it blue too.
Label where the number comes from: per utility contract in C4.
B14 still hides the price in =B6*0.13: rewrite it as =B6*B4, so the price lives in one place.
teach: F2 opens the cell for editing with the caret at the end — read a formula before you change it.

text: Rename Sheet2 to Inputs, delete Old wk37, and get a Report sheet in front.
Gridlines off on Report — someone reads this page.
State the units on Inputs: USD unless stated in A2.
Color the typed inputs B5 and B6 blue.
Put the wholesale price in B4 blue, label C4 per utility contract, and point the bill formula B14 at B4.
The questions are about the feed: move to Raw.
“How many days came through?” — jump to the last date with Ctrl+↓.
“Which columns does it carry?” — back to the top, then along the headers to F1.
“Is every energy cost in?” — ride Ctrl+↓ down column F; it stops at F11, right above the first missing figure.
“Anything below the feed?” — Ctrl+End to the far corner, Home, then up to the Notes header in A64.
teach: Ctrl+End jumps to the sheet’s last used cell, and Home snaps to column A of the row you are on.

text: Skim the feed a screen at a time: one PgUp, one PgDn.
teach: PgDn and PgUp move a screen at a time — for reading through, not for reaching a cell.

text: Back to the top for the next job: Ctrl+Home.
Move to Raw, where the selecting is.
Select Revenue from its header to the last figure: E1, then one Ctrl+Shift+↓.
Collapse to A1, then select the whole header row with Shift+Space.
teach: Shift+Space selects the active row; Ctrl+Space selects the active column.

text: Now the whole of column E with Ctrl+Space.
Select the whole feed in one press: Ctrl+A.
teach: Ctrl+A selects the current region — the block of data around the active cell.

text: Press Ctrl+A a second time: the entire sheet.
teach: Ctrl+A pressed again widens to the entire sheet.

text: Collapse to A1 with Ctrl+Home, then take everything used — feed, notes and the totals block — with Ctrl+Shift+End.
Warm up the tab keys: Ctrl+PgDn to Costs at the end, Ctrl+PgUp back to Report.
Management asks about the Airport Saturday: land on Raw!F61 in one jump.
teach: Ctrl+G (or F5) jumps to anything you can name — its job is far-off or cross-sheet targets, never the next cell over.

text: Select the whole Costs table by address: Costs!A3:E8.
teach: A sheet-qualified reference — Costs!A3:E8 — names the sheet, an exclamation mark, then the cell or range.

text: Hop home to Report on the tab keys, then land straight back on Costs!B7 in one jump.
Finish on the report page: Report!A1, one jump.
The question is about Costs: go there.
Select the table body B4:E8, edge to edge.
Pick out the constants — everything someone typed — and color them blue in one stroke.
teach: Go To Special (Alt, H, F, D, S) selects by kind inside your selection — O is Constants, F Formulas, Enter Blanks.

text: Select the body again and pick out the formulas — only the Domain total E4 lights up, and it stays black.
One more pass: the blanks — the two sites with no maintenance figure.
Land on the feed’s last date in one jump from the top of Raw.
Back to the top, then along the headers to the last column, F1.
Select everything used on the sheet from A1 in one stroke.
Select the Revenue figures E2:E60, edge to edge.
Go To Special, Constants — then color every typed number in the block blue.
Airport’s Saturday never came through: jump to the first blank cell of its row, Raw!C61.
Management emailed the day: enter 2,500 kWh in C61 and the price $0.48 in D61, moving right with Tab.
teach: Tab commits the entry and steps one cell right, and Excel remembers where the run began — that is where Enter will return you.

text: Finish the row with the revenue $1,200.00 in E61 and the energy cost $325.00 in F61, then Enter to land in C62.
teach: Enter after a Tab run commits and drops to the column the run started in, one row down — where the next record begins.

text: Start retyping the site name over B61, then look again — Airport is right, so discard the entry and keep it.
teach: Esc throws away an entry you have started: the cell keeps what it had, and nothing is committed.

text: Five Energy cost cells in column F are blank: select the feed from the top, pick out the blanks with Go To Special and count them.
Type 0 once and commit it into all five blank cells of the Energy cost column at the same time.
teach: Ctrl+Enter commits one entry into every selected cell at once — five blanks, one press.

text: A stray “draft” note sits in H3, above the site totals block: clear it.
teach: Delete clears what the cell holds and leaves its formatting behind — the italic stays for whatever is typed there next.

text: Does it tie? Watch Airport’s Saturday kWh in C61 change to 3,000 and the Airport line of the site totals, I12, answer.
Mueller is misspelled somewhere in the 60-row feed: move to Raw and find Muller.
teach: Ctrl+F opens Find: type part of what you want, Enter jumps to the next cell containing it, Esc closes the card.

text: Open B14 with F2, move the insertion point to just after Mu, and insert the e so it reads Mueller.
teach: In Edit mode, Home and End send the insertion point to either end of the entry and ← → step it one character; typing inserts there.

text: Riverside lost its e in one row: find Riversid, Find Next past the first hit (a correct Riverside), and add the e.
C33 shows 1,240 on the left — text with a trailing space: find it, open it, delete the space and commit it as a number.
teach: A figure sitting on the left is text, not a number; Backspace deletes the character before the insertion point, so the trailing space goes and 1,240 snaps right.

text: E41 reads 81500 for one day of South Lamar revenue when kWh × price says 1075: find it and type 1075 over it.
teach: Typing on a cell replaces its whole contents — no F2 when nothing in the old entry is worth keeping.

text: The associate asks what was there before: Ctrl+Z, and E41 shows 81500 again.
teach: Ctrl+Z undoes the last change and Ctrl+Y puts it back, so a fix can be tried, read and kept.

text: The figure was wrong after all: Ctrl+Y puts 1075 back in E41.
Does it tie? Watch C33, a Riverside kWh figure, change to 2,000 and Riverside’s kWh total in I10 answer.
Title the page: “Voltline - Austin Weekly KPI Report, w/c 15 Sep 2026” in A1, “USD unless stated” in A2, then Site and Week in A4:B4.
The feed’s totals block already carries the figure headers: copy Raw!I7:K7 and paste them onto C4:E4, then drop the marquee.
teach: Ctrl+C copies and Ctrl+X cuts the selection; Ctrl+V pastes it at the cursor, formats included; Esc drops the marquee, the moving border around what you copied.

text: The site list lives on Inputs: copy Inputs!A9:A13 and drop it under Site at A5 with Enter.
teach: After a copy, Enter pastes once and drops the marquee in the same press — the paste for a single destination.

text: Copy the reporting week from Inputs!B3 onto B5, then fill it down the five site rows B5:B9 with Ctrl+D.
teach: Ctrl+D fills the selection from its top row and Ctrl+R from its left column — one entry, filled, never retyped.

text: Label the daily block below the table: kWh sold by day in A12, then Week, Day and Date in A13:A15.
The daily block needs the same five sites: copy A5:A9 and drop them at A16 with Enter.
The daily block’s Week row takes the same label: copy it from B9 to B13, then fill it right across B13:G13 with Ctrl+R.
The Notes block sits under the feed where nobody reads it: cut Raw!A64:A67 and paste it beside the feed at H1.
Does it tie? Watch Domain’s Monday kWh in Raw!C8 change to 3,000 and Domain’s kWh total in I8 answer.
Two more figure columns are coming: type Gross profit ($) in F4 and Avg price ($/kWh) in G4 as one Tab run.
The associate wants last week beside this week: copy Raw’s Prior week rev and Old code block L7:M12 and paste values only onto H4.
teach: Paste Special, Ctrl+Alt+V, pastes one aspect of the copy — V values only, T formats only, E transposed — then Enter confirms.

text: Four new headers, one style: copy the kWh sold header C4 and paste its format only onto F4:I4 with Paste Formats.
Snapshot this week: copy the five sites’ live totals Raw!I8:K12 and paste values only onto C5, so the page holds numbers, not links.
Type Total in A10, then copy Raw’s total row I13:K13 and paste it plain onto C10: the SUM re-points to C5:C9.
teach: A pasted formula keeps its shape, not its cells: the references shift with the move, so =SUM(I8:I12) becomes =SUM(C5:C9) — a $ would pin them.

text: Start the sensitivity block under the daily table: Energy cost sensitivity ($/wk) in A22 and Price per kWh in A23.
The sensitivity table needs the sites across its top: copy A5:A9 and paste them transposed onto B23, one row of five.
Does it tie? Watch Domain’s Monday kWh in Raw’s C8 change: the live total I8 moves, and the Report’s snapshot C5 stays put.
Eleven cells on the Report still read w/c 08 Sep: swap every one for w/c 15 Sep with Replace All and read the count — eleven.
teach: Ctrl+H opens Replace: type what to find, Tab, what to put there, then Alt+A replaces every match on this sheet and reports how many cells changed.

text: Replace All only touches the active sheet: move to Inputs and replace the stale week label in B3 the same way — the count reads one.
One Airport row on the feed is spelled Airprot: move to Raw and find it with Ctrl+F.
Nothing in Airprot is worth keeping: type Airport over B55.
Back on the Report, the daily table needs its day header: type Mon in B14, select B14:G14 and let Fill Series carry it to Sat.
teach: Fill Series (Alt, H, F, I, S) continues the pattern your first cells set across the selection: Mon runs to Sat, 15 and 16 run on to 20.

text: The dates go under the days: type the first two, 15 and 16, into B15 and C15 as a Tab run.
Select B15:G15 and Fill Series carries 15 and 16 on to 20.
Does it tie? Watch Airport’s Monday kWh in Raw’s C56 change to 3,000 and the Airport line of the site totals, I12, answer.
Airport’s Saturday never came through: enter management’s figures in C61:F61 — 2,500 kWh, $0.48, $1,200.00 revenue and $325.00 energy cost.
Mueller is misspelled Muller in one row of the 60-row feed: find it and fix it in place.
Riverside reads Riverisde in three rows: Replace All of them in one step and read the count.
The kWh figure “1,240” in the Riverside rows was typed as text and sits on the left: make it a number.
Copy the site totals header H7:K7, insert a sheet named Summary in front, drop the header on its A1 and label E1 Snapshot.
With the feed complete, paste Raw’s site rows H8:K12 as values onto Summary!A2: a snapshot is values, never a live formula.
Under the snapshot, type Day in A8 and fill a Mon–Sat timeline across B8:G8.
Cedar Park opened this week: select Airport’s row 9 and insert a blank row above it — the Total in C11 follows to =SUM(C5:C10).
teach: Ctrl+Shift+= inserts whole rows or columns at the selection, Ctrl+- deletes them, and a SUM whose range straddles the insert grows to take the new row in.

text: Name the new site: type Cedar Park in A9, then fill the week label down from B8 into B9 with Ctrl+D.
Enter Cedar Park’s week across C9:E9 with Tab: 2,140 kWh, $1,005.80 revenue, $278.20 energy cost — the totals in C11:E11 grow together.
The Old code column is the old platform’s: select column I from its header I4 and delete the whole column in one press.
Margin % belongs before Prior week rev: insert a column at H and type Margin % in H4 — the header comes out bold.
On Raw, delete the Revenue column E and read the site totals block: every Revenue SUM now says #REF! instead of a number.
teach: #REF! means the formula pointed at a cell that no longer exists: delete a column a SUM reads and it breaks, and Ctrl+Z brings both back.

text: Read the error, then undo: Ctrl+Z brings the Revenue column back and Domain’s Revenue SUM in J8 reads a number again.
Does it tie? Watch Cedar Park’s kWh in C9 change to 3,000 and the Total in C11 answer.
The daily table’s six day columns B:G should share one width: select them from its timeline row and set Column Width 12.
teach: Column Width (Alt, H, O, W) sets every selected column to one width in Excel character units: select the columns first, then type the number and Enter.

text: Margin % and Prior week rev ($) in H:I are the comparison columns: select both from the header row and set them to 14.
Fit the label column to its site names, not the title: select A5:A11 and AutoFit — column A sizes to South Lamar.
teach: AutoFit Column Width (Alt, H, O, I) sizes a column to its content — a whole column fits everything in it, a selected range fits only those cells.

text: The title row is cramped at the default height: from A1, set Row Height 24 points.
teach: Row Height (Alt, H, O, H) sets the selected rows’ height in points; AutoFit Row Height (Alt, H, O, A) sizes a row back to its content.

text: Twenty-four was a guess: AutoFit Row Height puts row 1 back to what its one line of text needs.
At these widths the headers B4:I4 are clipped: select them from B4, wrap the text, then AutoFit row 4 to two lines.
teach: Wrap Text (Alt, H, W) folds a long entry onto more lines inside its cell, and AutoFit Row Height then sizes the row to the wrapped lines.

text: See why the day columns were set by hand: AutoFit B:G at once, read the uneven widths, then Ctrl+Z puts the equal 12 back.
Does it tie? Watch Cedar Park’s kWh in C9 change to 3,000 and the Total in C11 answer through the new widths.
Energy cost and Gross profit are working columns: select the whole of E:F from the header row and hide them with Ctrl+0.
teach: Ctrl+0 hides the selected columns and Ctrl+9 the rows; Ctrl+Shift+) and Ctrl+Shift+( unhide whatever is hidden inside the selection.

text: A buyer’s analyst will find a hidden column and wonder what else is hidden: select D:G across the gap and unhide with Ctrl+Shift+).
Rows hide the same way: select the whole daily table, rows 13:21, hide them with Ctrl+9, then bring them back with Ctrl+Shift+(.
Group, don’t hide: select the whole of E:F again and group the two working columns with Alt+Shift+→.
teach: Alt+Shift+→ groups the selected whole columns or rows into an outline with a button to fold and unfold; Alt+Shift+← ungroups them.

text: Fold the group with Hide Detail, Alt A H: the two columns tuck behind an outline button instead of vanishing.
Unfold it with Show Detail, Alt A J: the workings are there when a reader wants them, and the group stays.
The title, units, header row and site column must stay in view: land on B5 and freeze panes there with Alt W F F.
teach: Freeze Panes (Alt W F F) pins every row above and every column left of the active cell so they stay in view as the sheet scrolls.

text: Does it tie? Watch Cedar Park’s kWh in C9 change to 3,000 and the Total in C11 answer, with the heads frozen in place.
The Depot site opened: insert a row inside the block, above the last site, and enter Depot, 1,800 kWh, $828 revenue, $234 energy cost.
Old code in column H is the old platform’s site code: delete the whole column, not just its cells.
The six figure columns B:G are six different widths: select them from the header row and set Column Width 12.
A figure column is hidden — a buyer’s analyst would find it and wonder: unhide it inside the same selection.
Gross profit and Avg price in E:F are working columns: group them rather than hiding them.
Freeze the panes at B4 so the title, units, header row and site column stay in view.
Select the kWh sold figures C5:C11, Total included, and give them thousands separators with no decimals: Ctrl+1, then N.
teach: A number format changes how a value shows, not the value itself: Ctrl+1 opens Format Cells, whose categories answer to their first letter, N Number, C Currency, P Percentage.

text: Give Revenue, Energy cost and Gross profit D5:F11 comma style in one press, Ctrl+Shift+1, then Alt H 9 twice: negatives read in parentheses.
The $ goes on a money column’s first and total rows only: make D5:F5, D11:F11 and Prior week’s I5 currency with no decimals, Ctrl+1 then C.
Prior week rev I6:I10 gets thousands separators with no decimals, Cedar Park’s empty I9 included, while I5 keeps the column’s $.
Avg price ($/kWh) shows cents: select G5:G11 from the bottom, Ctrl+Shift+↑ then Shift+↓ off the header, and give it currency, Ctrl+Shift+4.
Margin % H5:H11 reads as a percentage to one decimal: select it the same way, Ctrl+Shift+5 for percent, then Alt H 0 for the decimal.
The daily table B17:G21 will hold thirty kWh figures: format the whole block at once, comma style with Ctrl+Shift+1, then Alt H 9 twice.
On Inputs, the wholesale energy price B4 is quoted to the tenth of a cent: currency with Ctrl+Shift+4, then Alt H 0 for the third decimal.
Does it tie? Watch Cedar Park’s kWh in C9 change to 3,000 and the Total in C11 answer, thousands separator and all.
The title in A1 is plain text: make it bold with Ctrl+B so the page has a heading.
teach: Ctrl+B makes the selection bold, Ctrl+I italic and Ctrl+U underlined; on a mixed selection it follows the active cell, so start from a plain cell and every cell goes on.

text: One font, one size, and the title is the one exception: take A1 one size up with Increase Font Size, Alt H F G.
Site and Week in A4:B4 were never bold: select the whole header row 4 with Shift+Space and one Ctrl+B bolds every header at once.
Jump down the site list to the Total in A11, select the whole row 11 with Shift+Space and make the total row bold.
A total takes a top border, never a grid: with row 11 still selected, add the top border with Alt H B P.
teach: The Borders menu is Alt H B, then a letter: P a top border, O a bottom, A all borders, N none.

text: On Inputs, the cells a reader may change are B3:B6: select the block and tint it light blue with Alt H H then Enter.
teach: Fill Color is Alt H H, then Enter for the light blue tint or arrows to another swatch; a fill marks a cell, never its value.

text: Does it tie? Watch Cedar Park’s kWh in C9 change to 3,000 and the Total in C11 answer, in bold above its top border.
The title in A1 belongs over the page: select A1:I1 and center it across the selection with Ctrl+1 then A, never Merge & Center.
teach: Center Across Selection (Ctrl+1, then A) centers a title over the selected columns without merging them; a merged cell breaks selection, fill and sorting.

text: A merged title would have stopped you here: go to A1 and press Ctrl+Shift+→ — the selection still sweeps along the row in one press.
Numbers align right, so their headers should too: select kWh sold through Prior week rev, C4:I4, and right-align them with Alt H A R.
teach: The alignment commands are Alt H A then a letter, L left, C center, R right; a header sits over its numbers when it is aligned the way they are.

text: The units line USD unless stated in A2 is a note, not a figure: make it italic with Ctrl+I so it reads as one.
The eight lines under kWh sold by day belong to it: jump to A13, select A14:A21 below it and indent them once with Alt H 6.
On Inputs, the source note per utility contract in C4 runs past its column: wrap it inside the cell with Alt H W.
Does it tie? Watch Cedar Park’s kWh in C9 change to 3,000 and the Total in C11 answer under the centered title.
On Costs, select the three cost columns B4:D8 and give them thousands separators with no decimals in one action, Ctrl+1 then N.
The Total column needs the same format: select E4:E8 and press F4 once; the whole Format Cells action you just did lands on all five cells.
teach: F4 outside a formula repeats your last action, a format, a border, a width, an insert, on whatever is selected now: format once, F4 everywhere.

text: The four headers B3:E3 sit over numbers, so right-align them with Alt H A R; Site in A3 sits over names and stays as it is.
Total ($/wk) is the column a reader looks for first: select E4:E8 again and make it bold with Ctrl+B.
A grid is not structure: select the whole block A3:E8 with Ctrl+A and take every border off with Alt H B N.
Does it tie? Watch Domain’s lease in B4 change to 2,500 and its Total in E4 answer, bold and with its thousands separator.
The figures C5:F10 are General with stray decimals: give them comma style, no decimals, and the Gross profit loss reads in parentheses.
Margin % in G5:G10 is a fraction: show it as a percentage to one decimal, Total included.
A grid of borders sits over the whole block A4:G10: remove every border from it, because a grid is not structure.
The Total row A10:G10 is a total: make it bold and give it a single top border.
Only the typed figures in C5:E9 are inputs: color them blue, and leave the formulas beside them in automatic black.
The title in A1 belongs over the page: center it across A1:G1 with Center Across Selection, never a merge.
Domain’s gross profit is revenue less energy cost: build =D5-E5 in F5 by pointing at the two cells with the arrow keys, not typing them.
teach: A formula starts with = and recalculates when its inputs change; while it is open, each arrow key points at a cell and writes its reference for you.

text: Domain’s average price is revenue divided by kWh: build =D5/C5 in G5 by pointing, jumping the pointer across the row with Ctrl+Left.
Domain’s margin is gross profit divided by revenue: build =F5/D5 in H5 the same way, with a Ctrl+Left jump to reach D5.
Read one back before you trust it: open F5 with F2 so its inputs D5 and E5 light up in color, then leave it unchanged.
Five sites still have no calculated lines: select F5:H10 with Domain’s three formulas at the top and fill them down with Ctrl+D.
The fill carried Domain’s $ sign down the gross-profit column: put F6:F10, and only those, back in comma style with no decimals.
Does it tie? Watch Domain’s kWh in C5 change to 3,000 and its average price in G5 answer.
Select the six sites’ figures C5:F10 and press Alt+= once: every column’s SUM lands in the total row, Gross profit’s F11 included.
teach: AutoSum, Alt+=, on one empty cell proposes a SUM over the numbers above; over a whole block it writes every column’s SUM into the row below in one press.

text: The total row needs its average price: G11 is total revenue over total kWh, D11 divided by C11, pointed the way the site rows were.
The total row needs its margin: H11 is total gross profit over total revenue, F11 divided by D11, pointed the same way.
Start a Week summary block under the report: Week summary in A26, bold, then the five line labels A27:A31 as one Enter run.
Type the first three lines: B27 =AVERAGE(C5:C10) for the average site, B28 =MAX(C5:C10) for the best, B29 =MIN(C5:C10) for the lowest.
teach: SUM, AVERAGE, MAX, MIN and COUNT each take one range, =AVERAGE(C5:C10), and a blank inside the range is left out, not counted as zero.

text: The three kWh lines B27:B29 read as figures: thousands separators and no decimals, the same comma format the report above uses.
Count the figures and the names: B30 =COUNT(C5:C10) counts the kWh figures, B31 =COUNTA(A5:A10) counts the site names.
teach: COUNT counts the numbers in a range and COUNTA counts every non-empty cell, text included, so COUNT checks the figures and COUNTA checks the names.

text: Does it tie? Watch Riverside’s kWh in C7 clear: the average in B27 and the count in B30 answer, and Sites listed in B31 does not.
Head the scenario grid: Energy cost at price ($/wk) in J3, bold, then the three prices 0.12, 0.13 and 0.14 across J4:L4 as one Tab run.
The prices are inputs, not headers: select J4:L4, switch off the bold row 4 gave them, color them blue, show them as currency, 2 decimals.
Domain’s cost at $0.12 is kWh times price: in J5 point at C5, F4 until it reads $C5, type *, point at J4, F4 until J$4.
teach: F4 inside an open formula cycles the anchors on the reference at the caret, C5, $C$5, C$5, $C5: a $ pins the column or row it sits before.

text: Give J5 thousands separators, no decimals, then fill it right across J5:L5 with Ctrl+R: $C5 stays on the kWh column, the price moves.
Now the five sites below: extend the selection to J5:L10 and fill down with Ctrl+D; J$4 stays on the price row while the kWh moves.
Read one from the middle of the grid before you trust it: open K7 with F2, see $C7 and K$4 lit in color, then Esc.
The old sensitivity stub under the daily block, a half-built what-if table, is covered by the grid now: select A23:F24 and clear it.
Does it tie? Watch the middle price in K4 change to $0.20 and every site’s cost under it, down to Airport’s K10, answer at once.
Domain’s kWh sold in C5 is a typed copy: replace it with a live link to Raw’s site total I8, pointing across sheets.
teach: A reference on another sheet names the sheet first, =Raw!I8: Ctrl+PgDn while the formula is open shows that sheet, and the arrows point there.

text: Mueller, Riverside and South Lamar follow: select C6:C8, point one link at Raw’s I9 and commit it into all three with Ctrl+Enter.
Revenue the same way: select D5:D8, point one link at Raw’s J8 and commit it into all four; the reference shifts a row per cell.
Airport sits below Cedar Park’s emailed row: select C10:D10, point at Raw’s I12 and Ctrl+Enter writes both links, kWh and revenue, at once.
Energy cost is kWh times the wholesale price on Inputs: select E5:E10, point =C5*Inputs!$B$4, anchor the price (F2, F4), Ctrl+Enter.
A link to another sheet is green in the format the team uses: color the energy costs E5:E10 green with Font Color, Alt H F C.
Format once, F4 everywhere: select C5:D8 and press F4 to repeat the green, then C10:D10, leaving Cedar Park’s typed C9:D9 automatic.
Does it tie? Watch the wholesale price on Inputs change to 0.200 and every energy cost in E5:E10, gross profit and margin answer.
Domain’s Monday in B17 is empty: link it to Domain’s Monday I32 in Raw’s by-day block, pointing across sheets.
Write the row once: with Monday’s link at the left of B17:G17, fill it right and all six days take the same pattern.
One of the associate’s cells is a number, not a link: show every formula in the daily table and find the one that stands out, E19.
teach: Ctrl+` shows every formula’s text in place of its value, so a typed number stands out from the links; press it again to return.

text: Riverside’s Thursday E19 was retyped: refill B19:G19 from its own Monday formula with F2 then Ctrl+Enter, never by retyping.
Bring the values back to the daily table: every cell in B17:G21 now reads as a live link.
A link to another sheet is shown green, the format the team uses: select B17:G17 and color Domain’s row with Alt H F C.
Does it tie? Watch Domain’s Monday kWh on Raw’s C8 change to 3,000 and the Report’s B17 answer through the by-day block.
On Costs, Mueller’s total E5 says #REF!, a reference that was deleted: replace the dead tail with a pointer to D5 so it reads =B5+C5+D5.
teach: Each error code is a message: #REF! a deleted reference, #NAME? a name Excel does not know, #VALUE! text where a number belongs, #N/A a lookup that found nothing.

text: E6 says #NAME?: SUMM is not a function Excel knows, so edit the name in place to SUM and the total reads 2,580 again.
E7 says #VALUE!: Ctrl+[ lands on B7, and along that row D7 says tbc where the flat 260 network fee belongs: fill it down from D6.
Airport’s E8 says #N/A and holds nothing worth keeping: select E5:E8, press F2 on E5, and Ctrl+Enter writes its formula into all four rows.
B10 now says #DIV/0!, a division by nothing: Ctrl+[ jumps to E9, Ctrl+] back, and it divides by the empty B12, so edit it to =E9/B11.
B11 is a link to the Report: press Ctrl+[ on it and the trail crosses sheets to Report’s C11, the kWh the cost is spread over.
Back on Costs, E5:E8 are formulas, not inputs, and must read black like E4: copy E4 and paste its format only onto them with Paste Formats.
Does it tie? Watch Domain’s lease in B4 change to 2,500 and the cost per kWh in B10 answer through the Total.
kWh sold in B5:B9 is typed from last week’s page: select B5:B9, point one link at Raw’s site total I8, then Ctrl+Enter.
Revenue in C5:C9 the same way, pointing at Raw’s J8, then color both link columns B5:C9 green: a link to another sheet is green.
Energy cost D5:D9 multiplies by a typed 0.13 and D8 is an error: put =B5*Inputs!$B$4, anchored with F4, into all five with Ctrl+Enter.
Gross profit E5:E9 mixes typed numbers, formulas and a #REF! in E7: select E5:E9, point =C5-D5 and commit it into every row with Ctrl+Enter.
The Total row B10:E10 is empty: select B5:E10, the block plus its blank edge, and one Alt+= writes every column’s SUM.
Margin % in F5:F10 is gross profit over revenue: select F5:F10, point =E5/C5 and commit it into all six rows with Ctrl+Enter.
Before you set the page, read how far it runs: jump to the last used cell, Z31, then come back to the top of the sheet.
A page wider than it is tall prints landscape: turn the Report with Alt P O L.
teach: Page Layout › Orientation, Alt P O then L for landscape or P for portrait, turns the printed page without opening a dialog box.

text: One page, however wide the columns run: open Page Setup, choose Fit to, leave the counts at 1 page wide by 1 tall, and OK it.
teach: Page Setup, Alt P S P, holds every print setting on its tabbed pages; F picks Fit to, one page wide by one page tall, and Enter is OK.

text: The title, the units line and the header row must top every printed page: set Print Titles to rows 1:4 with Alt P I.
teach: Print Titles, Alt P I, opens Page Setup on its Sheet page; the rows typed as Rows to repeat at top, 1:4, print at the top of every page.

text: A printed page must say which file it came from: on Page Setup’s Header/Footer page (Alt+H), put &[File] in the left footer section.
A printed page must also say when it was printed: on the Header/Footer page, Alt+R moves to the right section; put &[Date] there and OK it.
Does it tie? Watch Cedar Park’s kWh in C9 change to 3,000 and the Total in C11 answer: the print set-up changed nothing on the sheet.
Head a Checks block under the week summary: Checks in A33, bold, then the three check labels in A34:A36 as one Enter run.
In B34, take the five linked sites’ revenue D5:D8 and D10 and subtract the feed’s own total, pointing at Raw’s J13 across sheets.
teach: A check cell is a live difference between two things that must agree, so it reads 0 when they tie and shows the gap when they do not.

text: In B35, the six sites’ kWh must sum to the Total row: enter =SUM(C5:C10)-C11, and it reads 0 while the total row is honest.
In B36, a margin outside 0 to 100% is a mistake somewhere: enter =IF(AND(H11>=0,H11<=1),0,1), which reads 0 while the margin is plausible.
Give the three checks B34:B36 the figures’ format, comma style with no decimals, so all three read a plain 0.
A reviewer will ask what the first check compares: from B34, Ctrl+[ follows the trail to D5, the first revenue figure it reads.
Does it tie? Watch a number typed over Mueller’s revenue link in D6 and the revenue check in B34 leave zero: the break is caught.
Typed numbers hide among the links: select C5:E10, run Go To Special for Constants, and color Cedar Park’s emailed figures blue.
teach: The audit pass is three looks: Go To Special for typed numbers among links, show formulas for a number in a formula row, the page for the rest.

text: E9 multiplies the emailed kWh, so the whole Cedar Park row is marked blue until the feed carries the site: move to E9 and press F4.
Mueller’s average price G6 divides by a typed 6850, which Ctrl+` shows at a glance: rewrite it as =D6/C6 by pointing.
In the daily table Mueller’s Thursday E18 is a number in a formula row: select B18:G18, F2 on the link in G18, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+` off.
Prior week rev is hidden between H and J, and a buyer who finds one hidden column looks for more: select H:J and press Ctrl+Shift+).
The title was centered by typing spaces in front of it: retype it in A1 without them, then center it across A1:I1 with Ctrl+1 then A.
The units line is gone, so a reader cannot tell which currency the figures are in: in A2 press Ctrl+I, then type USD unless stated.
A grid sits over the daily table with gridlines on: select B15:G21, take every border off with Alt H B N, then Alt W V G.
Does it tie? Watch Cedar Park’s kWh in C9 change to 3,000 and the Total in C11 answer: the page is clean and still live.
The title was centered with spaces and the units line is gone: delete the spaces, center A1 across A1:I1, restore USD unless stated in A2.
Cedar Park’s emailed figures sit black among the green links: Go To Special constants over C5:D10 finds them; color them blue.
Show formulas: one Avg price cell divides by a typed kWh figure, so rewrite G5:G10 as one formula, =D5/C5, with Ctrl+Enter.
A grid was drawn over the daily table B15:G21 with the gridlines on: remove every border and turn the gridlines off.
One daily-table cell is a typed number among links: select B17:G21, open B17 with F2, commit it to every cell with Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+` off.
The page prints landscape on one sheet but carries no page number: put Page &[Page] of &[Pages] in the center footer section.
Give the page its title in A1, bold and one size up, and the units line USD unless stated in A2 in italic.
Tab the eight headers, Site to Margin %, into A4:H4; bold them, right-align and wrap C4:H4, then center the title across A1:H1.
Copy the five site names from Inputs A9:A13 into A5:A9, then type the week label w/c 22 Sep in B5 and fill it down to B9.
Point C5 and D5 at Raw’s I8 and J8 across sheets, E5 at C5 × the wholesale price on Inputs anchored, all three green.
Point Domain’s gross profit F5 =D5-E5, average price G5 =D5/C5 and margin H5 =F5/D5, one after another with Tab.
Row 5 is the page’s one formula row: select C5:H9 with Ctrl+Shift+End and fill it down the five sites with Ctrl+D.
Select C5:F10, the block plus its blank edge: one Alt+= totals every column; point G10 =D10/C10 and H10 =F10/D10; type Total in A10.
Format C5:F10 comma style with no decimals, G5:G10 currency 2, H5:H10 percent 1, then currency 0 on D5:F5 and again on D10:F10 with F4.
The Total row is bold with a top border, never a grid: select the whole row 10 with Shift+Space, Ctrl+B, then Alt H B P.
Head the daily block: A12 kWh sold by day bold, A13:G13 Site and Mon to Sat bold with the days right-aligned, A14:A18 the sites indented.
Select A13:G18, Go To Special for Blanks, point one link at Raw’s I32 and Ctrl+Enter fills all thirty cells; comma 0, green.
Head a Checks block at A20 with its three labels, then the three checks in B21:B23 reading 0, the first pointed at Raw’s J13, comma 0.
Set columns B:F to width 12 and G:H to 14, then AutoFit column A to its site names A5:A18 and row 4 to its wrapped headers.
Freeze panes at B5, gridlines off, then set the page to print: landscape, one page, rows 1:4 repeated, &[File] and &[Date] in the footer.
Does it tie? Watch Domain’s Monday kWh on Raw change to 3,000 and the Total in C10 answer while the checks in B21:B23 stay zero.
A1: Voltline - City Weekly KPI Report, w/c 22 Sep 2026, with the city as Costs A1 names it; A2: USD unless stated.
Row 4, bold: Site, Week, kWh sold, Revenue ($), Energy cost ($), Gross profit ($), Avg price ($/kWh), Margin % across A4:H4.
The five sites from Inputs A9:A13 into A5:A9, and the week label w/c 22 Sep in B5:B9.
kWh sold and revenue C5:D9 as live links to Raw’s site totals I8:J12, pointed across sheets.
Energy cost E5:E9 is kWh times the wholesale price, =C5*Inputs!$B$4 anchored, then color every link C5:E9 green.
F5:F9 =D5-E5, G5:G9 =D5/C5, H5:H9 =F5/D5 filled down; Total in A10, C10:F10 by AutoSum, G10 =D10/C10, H10 =F10/D10.

Does it tie? Watch the first site’s Monday kWh on Raw change to 3,000 and the Report’s total in C10 answer while the checks stay zero.
The Report shows its gridlines: turn them off, as a page someone reads should be.
Every week label on the Report still reads w/c 08 Sep: replace all of them with w/c 15 Sep in one pass.
The panes are unfrozen, so the headers scroll away: freeze them at B5 so rows 1–4 and column A stay in view.
The second site’s revenue in D6 is a typed number where its link belongs: make it =Raw!J9 again.
The average prices in G5:G11 lost their format: show them as currency with two decimals.
Margin % is hidden between G and I: select G:I and unhide it.
The gross-profit total in F11 was retyped as a number: make it =SUM(F5:F10) again.
On Inputs the wholesale price in B4 is an input shown black: color it blue.
On Costs the typed figures in B4:D8 read black: select the constants with Go To Special and color them blue.
On Raw the site name in B14 has a doubled last letter: open it and remove the extra letter.
